newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway stock up with Wall Street gains from Friday.
newsitem.headline: Norway stock up with Wall Street gains from Friday.

text.p: Norwegian shares firmed on Monday to catch up with a pre-weekend rally on Wall Street with industrial conglomerate Norsk Hydro being the most traded share.
Oslo's Total share index finished 1.18 percent higher at 1,012.86 points. Turnover was brisk at 972 million crowns, 119 million crowns of which was attributed to Norsk Hydro.
The share, which has a 20 percent weighting on the bourse, rose 1.27 percent to 358.50 crowns.
The rise of the crown continued to hurt export-orinented stock such as metals maker Elkem and forestry group Norske Skogindustrier, both of which fell on the bourse.
Dealers said sentiment was uncertain and the market was expected to drift under the influence of the continuing strength of the crown and lower interest rates.

"Today we're up because Wall Street was up when everyone expected it to be down," said an Oslo-based broker. "But the situation in Norway is a double-edge sword at the moment with the crown getting stronger and stronger and interest rates getting lower. The market's being pulled in both directions."
Norway's central bank lowered its key interest rates twice in two days last week to try and dampen the crown's rise. The petrocurrency continued upwards on Monday.
